# monitorable_server_mute (Resource)

A maintenance mute on a server's alerts. Set `until` for a window; omit it to mute until the resource is destroyed. A mute whose `until` has passed stays in state as completed and is not re-applied; change `until` to open a new window. Destroying the resource unmutes the server. Declare at most one `monitorable_server_mute` per server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "monitorable_server" "web" {
  name = "web-01"
}

# A maintenance window: alerts are muted until the instant passes. After that
# the resource stays in state as completed (active = false) and is not applied
# again; change `until` to open a new window.
resource "monitorable_server_mute" "window" {
  server_id = monitorable_server.web.id
  until     = "2026-12-01T06:00:00Z"
  reason    = "kernel upgrade"
}

# Mute for the duration of one apply, for example from a deploy pipeline.
# timestamp() changes on every run, so ignore_changes keeps the mute from being
# replaced by the next plan: the window is opened once, when the resource is
# created, and `terraform destroy` lifts it early. A pipeline that wants one
# window per deploy should drop `ignore_changes`: each apply's timestamp() then
# differs from the state's, which replaces the mute and opens a fresh window.
resource "monitorable_server_mute" "deploy" {
  server_id = monitorable_server.web.id
  until     = timeadd(timestamp(), "30m")
  reason    = "deploy"

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [until]
  }
}

# With no `until` the mute lasts until the resource is destroyed.
resource "monitorable_server_mute" "until_destroyed" {
  server_id = monitorable_server.web.id
  reason    = "decommissioning"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_id` (String) The id of the server to mute, a decimal integer. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `reason` (String) Why the server is muted, at most 200 characters, shown in the dashboard. It must not start or end with whitespace or contain control characters. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `until` (String) When the mute ends (RFC 3339; any offset, compared as an instant). Omit it to mute until the resource is destroyed. It must be in the future when the mute is created, and at most 366 days ahead. Changing it to another instant replaces the resource, which opens a new window. A window lifted early in the dashboard is re-created on the next apply only while `until` is still in the future; once it has passed, the resource is a completed record and is left alone.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the server is muted now, as the API reports it. Once the window has passed the resource stays in state as completed and `active` still mirrors the API: it is false unless someone has muted the server again since.
- `id` (String) The server id; a server has at most one mute.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the server id. A server that is not muted has no mute to import.
terraform import monitorable_server_mute.window 42
```
